title: Packages, import rules and what a capital letter means

videos.script: Lesson 38 gave a module a name and a dependency, and kept all of its code in one directory. This lesson splits the code. {{tree}} First the shape. A small module with two programs and a library they share, laid out the way the Go toolchain lays out its own source. Section 02 shows that a package is a directory, and that its import path is the module's path plus that directory. {{capital}} Then the capital letter lesson 4 pointed at. Three calls that reach into another package, and three refusals. Lesson 15's missing JSON field turns out to be the same rule. {{rules}} Last, what an import may not do. Two packages that import each other, and a package another module is not allowed to see. Then the four ways to write an import, including one that runs code you never call. By the end, you can split a program into packages and say who is allowed to use each name.
